skill.name: web-fetch
skill.description: Fetch public web pages and convert the main content to clean Markdown using curl, html2markdown, and a Bun fallback parser.
skill.summary: Turns documentation and articles into clean Markdown for AI context.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: The TypeScript backtick findings are false positives from template literals that format Markdown and logs. The skill still intentionally fetches arbitrary URLs and includes shell workflows using curl, html2markdown, and Bun. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Validate URLs before fetching. Allow only http and https, and block localhost, link-local, and private network ranges by default.

remediation.issue: Pasteable shell commands use raw URL placeholders
remediation.suggestion: Move URL handling into a reviewed script that receives arguments safely. Avoid asking agents to interpolate untrusted text into shell snippets.
Ship a lockfile and pinned dependencies. Prefer installation during skill setup, not during normal task execution.

remediation.issue: Network shell workflows require user awareness
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before fetching user-supplied URLs, especially for internal domains or authenticated environments.

content.value_statement: Teams often need web pages as clean Markdown for AI context. This skill fetches pages, selects main content, and removes common navigation noise.
actual_capabilities: Checks page content type before choosing a Markdown or HTML extraction path.
Uses curl and html2markdown examples for selector-based page extraction.
Provides selectors for Anthropic, Claude, MDN, GitHub, and generic documentation pages.
Runs a bundled Bun parser when command-line selectors produce poor output.
Removes common navigation, header, footer, script, style, and copy-button content.
limitations: Requires curl, html2markdown, and Bun for the full workflow.
Does not render JavaScript-only pages or browser-dependent content.
Can fetch only URLs reachable from the local execution environment.
Selector quality may vary by site structure and page template.

use_cases.title: Collect API Documentation
use_cases.description: Fetch a public documentation page and convert the main article into Markdown for model context.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Notes
use_cases.description: Extract readable article content from public pages before summarizing findings or comparing sources.

use_cases.title: Clean Reference Material
use_cases.description: Remove navigation and layout noise from source pages before drafting guides or support answers.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this documentation page as clean Markdown: <url>

prompt_templates.title: Prefer Main Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with extraction quality guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch <url>, prefer a Markdown-native response, and remove navigation before summarizing the main content.

prompt_templates.title: Test Selectors
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for pages with noisy layouts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch <url>, test the best include selector, and return clean Markdown plus a short note on selector quality.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch these URLs: <url list>. For each page, choose markdown-native, selector extraction, or Bun fallback, then compare key differences.

output_examples.output: Clean Markdown with the article title, headings, paragraphs, and examples while navigation is removed.
A readable Markdown document focused on the content container, with sidebars and headers removed.

output_examples.input: Fetch a page where generic selectors fail.
output_examples.output: Main content extracted by the Bun fallback, followed by a note that JavaScript-only sections may be missing.

best_practices: Confirm the URL is expected and public before fetching it.
Prefer markdown-native endpoints when the content type supports them.
Use narrow selectors when generic extraction includes navigation or sidebars.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch private, localhost, or internal network URLs.
Do not paste untrusted URLs into shell commands without careful quoting.
Do not rely on this skill for JavaScript-rendered pages.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: curl is required. html2markdown and Bun are needed for selector extraction and fallback parsing.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it fetch private websites?
faq.answer: It can only fetch URLs reachable from your environment. Private sites may require separate authenticated access.

faq.question: Does it run a browser?
faq.answer: No. It uses curl, html2markdown, and a Bun parser. It cannot render browser-only content.

faq.question: How does it choose content?
faq.answer: It prefers Markdown responses, then selectors such as article, main, or role main, then the Bun fallback.

faq.question: What security review is needed?
faq.answer: Review URLs before fetching and avoid internal hosts. Community skills with shell commands should require confirmation.
